newsitem.title: INDIA: India Eicher in 2 bln rupee expansion.
newsitem.headline: India Eicher in 2 bln rupee expansion.

text.p: India's Eicher group will invest 2.0 billion rupees in an expansion project to make motorcycles, tractors, trucks and automobile components including gears, group chairman Subodh Bhargava told a news conference on Tuesday.
He said more than half of the investment would be in truck maker Eicher Motors Ltd, while the rest would be invested by Eicher Ltd.
"Auto components is something bigger we are looking for," said Bhargava, who said the 2.0 billion rupee expansion beginning in early 1998 would take two years to implement.
The expansion project would involve a 400 million rupee investment to make tractors of 61 horsepower (HP) capacity with technology from Finland's Valmet Oy, Bhargava said.
This would be in addition to an ongoing 2.0 billion rupee expansion project involving 700 million rupees of investment in trucks and 1.3 billion in Eicher Ltd, he said.

Eicher Tractors Ltd was merged in 1995 into Eicher Ltd, which has other separate divisions to make motorcycles and gears. The Eicher group holds 60.5 percent in the company, in which financial institutions and the public hold the rest.
Japan's Mitsubishi Motors Corp holds a minority stake of 7.5 percent in Eicher Motors, in which the Eicher group holds 44.5 percent. Financial institutions and the general public hold the rest.
